title: Fortran Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Write a greeting
examples.description: A program block holds the steps. The A format writes character text.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none

write(*,'(A)') "Hello, Asha!"
end program lesson

examples.title: Name a whole number
examples.description: integer declares a whole-number value. The I0 format prints it without leading padding.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: pencils = 3
write(*,'(I0)') pencils + 2
end program lesson

examples.title: Use a decimal value
examples.description: real holds a decimal value. The F3.1 format prints one digit after the decimal point.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
real :: length = 2.5
write(*,'(F3.1)') length
end program lesson

examples.title: Group numbers in an array
examples.description: An array stores several values. This array has three integer positions.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson

examples.title: Read an array position
examples.description: Fortran arrays normally start at position 1. Parentheses select an item.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(I0)') scores(2)
end program lesson

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: An if block runs one branch based on a logical test.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: score = 8
if (score >= 5) then
 write(*,'(A)') "Pass"
else
 write(*,'(A)') "Try again"
end if
end program lesson

examples.title: Count with do
examples.description: A counted do loop includes both its start and end values.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: n
do n = 1, 3
 write(*,'(I0)') n
end do
end program lesson

examples.title: Add an array
examples.description: sum adds the values in an array. It is a built-in array operation.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: values(3) = [2, 3, 4]
write(*,'(I0)') sum(values)
end program lesson

examples.title: Change selected array items
examples.description: where applies a change only where an array condition is true.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 8, 9]
where (scores >= 7) scores = scores + 1
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson

examples.title: Return a calculated value
examples.description: A function has a result. contains separates the main steps from local function definitions.
examples.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 write(*,'(I0)') twice(4)
contains
 integer function twice(n) result(answer)
  integer, intent(in) :: n
  answer = n * 2
 end function twice
end program lesson

examples.title: Change a value through a subroutine
examples.description: A subroutine is called with call. intent(inout) means this input may be changed.
examples.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 integer :: n = 4
 call double_value(n)
 write(*,'(I0)') n
contains
 subroutine double_value(value)
  integer, intent(inout) :: value
  value = value * 2
 end subroutine double_value
end program lesson

examples.title: Choose an array size at run time
examples.description: An allocatable array gets its size when allocate runs. deallocate releases its storage.
examples.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer, allocatable :: scores(:)
allocate(scores(3))
scores = 0
write(*,'(I0)') size(scores)
deallocate(scores)
end program lesson
